title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Explore the distinct corridors and districts surrounding Duke University, from the historic Ninth Street to the industrial-chic American Tobacco Campus.

cards.title: Ninth Street
cards.subtitle: Ninth Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the Regulator Bookshop for local reads or grab a scratch-made donut at Monuts in this historic district just blocks from East Campus.
cards.short_summary: The primary off-campus commercial hub for Duke students, featuring local bookstores, cafes, and independent retail.
cards.evidence_claim: Ninth Street is described as the social center of off-campus Duke life and a walkable strip packed with restaurants and shops.
cards.source_title: Neighborhood Guide: Ninth Street - nearDuke Off-Campus Guide
cards.access_notes: Public street with various business hours; Monuts is open until 9:00 PM Tuesday-Saturday.

cards.title: Brightleaf Square
cards.subtitle: West Main Street
cards.notes: Explore repurposed tobacco warehouses housing Rose's Noodles and Jeni's Splendid Ice Creams in this historic Romanesque brick district.
cards.short_summary: A historic district of renovated tobacco warehouses featuring upscale dining, retail, and courtyard spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Brightleaf Square is a main hub for restaurants and shopping in the west end of downtown Durham, close to Duke's East Campus.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; courtyard is accessible to the public; individual business hours vary.

cards.title: Erwin Road
cards.subtitle: Erwin Road Corridor
cards.notes: Walk to Enzo's Pizza or Chipotle from the Lofts at Lakeview in this high-density residential area adjacent to Duke Medical Center.
cards.short_summary: A major thoroughfare bordering West Campus and the Medical Center, lined with student-oriented apartments and fast-casual dining.
cards.evidence_claim: Erwin Road is a primary residential area for Duke students, featuring complexes like Lofts at Lakeview and various dining options.
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; businesses typically open until 10:00 PM or later.

cards.title: Broad Street
cards.subtitle: Broad Street Corridor
cards.notes: Grab a coffee at Joe Van Gogh or shop at the local Whole Foods in this quieter alternative to the Ninth Street bustle.
cards.short_summary: A commercial corridor parallel to Ninth Street offering local coffee shops and essential grocery services.
cards.evidence_claim: Broad Street is home to Joe Van Gogh coffee and is a popular weekend stop for students and locals.
cards.access_notes: Public street; Joe Van Gogh is a popular study spot for students.

cards.title: Foster Street
cards.subtitle: Central Park District
cards.notes: Visit the Durham Farmers Market on Saturday mornings or explore the Durham Food Hall in this vibrant arts and recreation district.
cards.short_summary: The heart of Durham's Central Park district, known for its weekly farmers market and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: Foster Street is the location of Durham Central Park and the Durham Farmers Market, serving as a community hub.
cards.access_notes: Farmers Market open Saturdays 8am-12pm; park is open daily.

cards.title: Geer Street
cards.subtitle: Geer Street Corridor
cards.notes: Check out the murals at GeerHouse or grab a coffee at Cocoa Cinnamon in this rapidly developing industrial-style neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: A trendy district north of downtown featuring historic service stations converted into cafes and restaurants.
cards.evidence_claim: Geer Street features local favorites like Cocoa Cinnamon and Geer Street Garden, often housed in repurposed historic buildings.
cards.access_notes: Public street; Cocoa Cinnamon is a popular student hangout.

cards.title: American Tobacco Campus
cards.subtitle: Blackwell Street
cards.notes: Walk along the man-made river or catch a Durham Bulls game next door at this massive historic factory redevelopment.
cards.short_summary: A premier mixed-use destination featuring offices, restaurants, and the iconic Lucky Strike water tower.
cards.evidence_claim: The American Tobacco Campus is a historic redevelopment with over a million square feet of space, including restaurants and green space.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public 24/7; security on-site; individual business hours vary.

cards.title: West Main Street
cards.subtitle: Downtown Main Street
cards.notes: Dine at local staples like Devine's Restaurant or explore the shops connecting the Brightleaf District to the city center.
cards.short_summary: The primary east-west artery of downtown Durham, connecting Duke's East Campus to the central business district.
cards.evidence_claim: West Main Street is a key corridor featuring long-standing businesses like Devine's and connecting major districts.
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; Devine's is open late for sports viewing.

cards.title: University Hill
cards.subtitle: University Drive
cards.notes: View the UHILL Walls, one of the largest mural collections in the Southeast, while visiting local eateries in this mixed-use development.
cards.short_summary: A modern mixed-use development known for its extensive mural art and diverse food and drink options.
cards.evidence_claim: University Hill features over 35 murals and 8+ food and drink establishments within a 300,000 square foot development.
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible mural walk; retail hours vary.

cards.title: Gregson Street
cards.subtitle: Trinity Park / Downtown
cards.notes: Visit The Can Opener food truck park near the famous low-clearance bridge for local eats and outdoor games.
cards.short_summary: A corridor bordering Trinity Park featuring new community-focused dining concepts and the infamous 'Can Opener' bridge.
cards.evidence_claim: The Can Opener on Gregson Street is a food truck park offering a variety of local vendors and outdoor seating.
cards.access_notes: Open daily 7:00 AM - 10:00 PM; food truck hours may vary.
